body: Material remains, oral histories and written records give different kinds of evidence about people in the past. A tool can show manufacturing choices. An oral account can preserve names and relationships. A written account can record transactions, while expressing its author's interests and point of view.

Fossil and genetic evidence place the origin of Homo sapiens in Africa. Agricultural histories vary by region. Archaeologists have evidence for local plant domestication in eastern North America, and clay tablets from ancient Mesopotamia document one early writing tradition. These examples answer different historical questions and belong to different regional timelines.

Spaceflight examples have more precise recorded dates. Sputnik 1 became the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth in 1957. In 1969 the Apollo 11 crew carried out the first human landing on the Moon.

limitations: Surviving evidence is unevenly distributed. New findings can change an interpretation, and a few examples cannot represent all historical experiences.
purpose: Introduce historical comparison through material evidence and social context.
